description: OS-level memory management decomposed. Anon vs file pages. kswapd background reclaim. Direct reclaim. Page tables, swap, zswap. The OOM killer's scoring algorithm. Why agents get killed under memory pressure + how to influence the outcome.

sub_mechanisms.name: anonymous_pages
sub_mechanisms.definition: Memory not backed by a file: heap, stack, anonymous mmap. Must be saved to swap if reclaimed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Heap + stack is anon. Can't just drop — would lose data. Reclaim writes to swap. No swap = anon pages can't be reclaimed (only OOM-killed).

sub_mechanisms.name: file_backed_pages
sub_mechanisms.definition: Memory backed by a file: page cache, executable text, mmap'd files. Reclaimable by dropping (if clean) or writing back (if dirty).
sub_mechanisms.why: Cheap to reclaim: just discard. Source from disk on next access. The 'free' memory shown by free(1) is mostly reclaimable file-backed pages.

sub_mechanisms.name: kswapd
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-NUMA-node kernel thread that reclaims pages in the background when free memory falls below watermarks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Proactive reclaim avoids waiting for memory at allocation time. Wakes when free pages < watermark_low; sleeps when > watermark_high. Keeps the system responsive under moderate pressure.

sub_mechanisms.name: direct_reclaim
sub_mechanisms.definition: Synchronous reclaim during page allocation. If kswapd can't keep up, the allocator itself reclaims pages.
sub_mechanisms.why: Last resort before allocation failure. Visible as latency spikes in applications. PSI exposes time spent in direct reclaim. Mitigate by tuning vm.watermark_scale_factor (start kswapd earlier).

sub_mechanisms.name: watermark_min_low_high
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-zone watermarks: min (allocator failure threshold), low (kswapd wakes), high (kswapd stops). kswapd reclaims until > high.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hysteresis: avoid kswapd thrashing. The gap between low + high is configurable. Larger gap = less thrashing but coarser response.

sub_mechanisms.name: page_LRU_lists
sub_mechanisms.definition: Two-list LRU per zone: active + inactive. Pages promoted from inactive to active on second reference. Reclaim from inactive list.
sub_mechanisms.why: Avoids reclaiming recently-accessed pages. Working set lives in active list; truly cold pages in inactive. Approximates true LRU at much lower cost (no list manipulation on every access).

sub_mechanisms.name: shrinker_callbacks
sub_mechanisms.definition: Kernel subsystems register shrinkers: callbacks to free their caches under pressure. dcache, inode cache, slab caches.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reclaim isn't just user pages — kernel caches grow too. Shrinkers let each subsystem decide how much to free. Called proportionally to memory pressure.

sub_mechanisms.name: swap_to_disk
sub_mechanisms.definition: Anon pages written to swap partition or file when reclaimed. Restored on next access (page fault → swap-in).
sub_mechanisms.why: Extends virtual memory beyond RAM. Cost: disk-level latency for swapped-in pages. Most modern systems use swap conservatively — too much swap = thrashing + system unresponsive.

sub_mechanisms.name: zswap_compressed_swap
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compress anon pages in RAM as a 'swap cache' before writing to disk. zstd or LZ4 compression.
sub_mechanisms.why: Trade compute for capacity. 50% compression effectively doubles usable RAM for anon-heavy workloads. Default on many distros; particularly useful on memory-constrained containers/VMs.

sub_mechanisms.name: OOM_score_adj
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-process tunable: -1000 (never kill) to +1000 (kill first). Added to oom_score (RSS-based) to influence killer choice.
sub_mechanisms.why: User-settable OOM victim preference. systemd services can have OOMScoreAdjust= setting. Critical services get -500 or lower; sacrificial work gets +500.

sub_mechanisms.name: OOM_killer_algorithm
sub_mechanisms.definition: On OOM: iterate processes; pick highest oom_score (with adj). Kill it. Repeat if still OOM.
sub_mechanisms.why: Heuristic: kill largest-uses-most. Often correct (biggest process freed = most memory). Wrong on some workloads (kill the database). Pre-emptive userspace OOM (oomd, earlyoom) lets policy override the kernel's heuristic.

sub_mechanisms.name: memory_cgroup_OOM
sub_mechanisms.definition: When a cgroup's memory.max is breached, OOM-killer kills within the cgroup, not system-wide.
sub_mechanisms.why: Container memory limit reached → kill in container, not host's processes. memory.oom.group lets the whole cgroup be killed (useful for distributed-systems-aware workloads).

derivation_rules.name: kswapd_proactive_reclaim_avoids_allocation_stalls
if: kswapd keeps free memory above the low watermark
derivation_rules.why: Direct reclaim blocks the allocating process. kswapd's background reclaim keeps memory ready. Tuning watermark_scale_factor higher gives more buffer at the cost of running kswapd more eagerly.

derivation_rules.name: anon_without_swap_uncreclaimable
if: system has no swap and is anon-heavy
then: anon pages can't be reclaimed; only file pages free up
derivation_rules.why: Anon pages have nowhere to go without swap. Heap, stack stay in RAM until process exits. Heavy anon allocation under memory pressure → OOM faster than systems with swap. Container with no swap + memory.max = brittle.

derivation_rules.name: OOM_score_adj_lets_admin_override_heuristic
then: it's much less likely to be killed than larger processes
derivation_rules.why: oom_score_adj effectively reduces oom_score by adj * (memory_size / 1000). Critical processes at -500 require very high RSS share to be killed. Standard production tuning for important daemons.

derivation_rules.name: page_LRU_approximates_true_LRU_cheaply
if: pages reside in active or inactive lists
then: frequently-accessed pages are protected from reclaim
derivation_rules.why: True LRU requires moving each accessed page to MRU position — expensive. Two-list LRU just needs to mark accessed; second access promotes. Approximates LRU at constant per-access cost.

derivation_rules.name: memory_cgroup_OOM_contains_blast_radius
then: OOM-kill happens within the cgroup, not system-wide
derivation_rules.why: Without per-cgroup OOM, runaway container would trigger host-wide OOM-kill, possibly killing other services. Per-cgroup containment isolates the failure. Critical for multi-tenant hosts (Kubernetes nodes).
